Ask HN: What will happen if AI is mature and people have little work to do?
item.description:
Three years ago I asked the same question (https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=35327092), and the landscape has changed since then. Just say that even the most AI skepticism people will have to admit that with recent models, even open source ones, LLM is already a valuable intelligence resource, at least in the right hands. Of course we are nowhere near AGI yet, but no theorem can assert that AI will not be at least as good as human; neuro-networks can fit arbitrarily complex function. If human thought, based on the physical structure of brain, is computable, then some computer program can certainly take advantage of that. Even if there is some weird physics that yields non-computable properties, there is also no stop of building such a computer to take advantage of that law and thus have an AI on top of it too.

Some disciplines are invulnerable to AIs, such as math or art, where human comprehension and expression is the product itself. But how about others such as engineering where "if it works it works"? There are certainly engineers who love engineering but instead of "here is some AI tools that lets you focus on your main, non-trivial tasks", they are getting "you can certainly do that, but AI will complete faster and with less money". (A lot of people had trivial work that can already largely be replaced by AI by now.) AI might take a large portion of fun out of these fields. Maybe they will degrade to sports or specialized handcrafts, just like running (sports) or sewing (handcrafts) in modern world.

I wrote https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49578280#49579794 several days ago, but on second thought I can't even convince myself. We have to admit that sometimes we want to do something because it is hard, or never done before. External incentives are also totally valid options.

Ask HN: What if we funded math research like we fund AI labs?
item.description:
The annual U.S. federal budget for basic math research is <$1B.

OpenAI alone just raised ~$122B, and frontier labs are increasingly concentrating enormous amounts of compute and human talent on open math problems.

We seem to be entering a strange situation where a handful of private labs have vastly more resources for attacking these problems than the academics traditionally responsible for doing so.

Have we had the capability all along, just not the hype? Please discuss :)

Show HN: Toolcraft – open-source AI harness and starter for building design apps
item.description:
MIT-licensed, 100% free starter kit, UI library, and AI harness for building your own design apps. Works with Codex, Claude, Cursor, or any other agents.

I’ve always been passionate about pushing the boundaries of design software, spending years with tools like Figma, Blender, After Effects, Photoshop, and Illustrator. But some design tasks need different software — tailored exactly to your needs and creative vision. Apps that aren’t vendor-locked. Apps you can freely modify to make your workflow faster and better.

A year ago I started building design apps for the projects I was working on, but I was always starting from scratch or babysitting AI over and over again just to get a proper canvas, controls, toolbar or timeline. That took time. Plus AI sucks at design, so the components it spat out were usually terrible.

I wanted to work in an environment I’d actually love to spend my workdays in, so I designed and built Toolcraft.

What Toolcraft includes - A starter app built with TanStack Router, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and Base UI - A canvas with the familiar pan and zoom controls you’d expect from a design tool - A component library with buttons, dropdowns, sliders, font pickers, color palettes, curve editors, image uploaders, and more - Built-in layers, animation timelines, and keyframes that your agent can turn on as your app needs them. - Image and video export workflows - An AI harness that gives your agent the skills, instructions, and checks to build on Toolcraft’s design system. - Unit, browser, acceptance, and performance checks - All the code behind your app, ready to customize with your AI agent

What can you use Toolcraft for: - Procedural graphics and gradient generators - Image stylization, ASCII, pixel, halftone, and glitch effects - Shader and Three.js experiments - Animation and video-effect tools - Blog cover and branded asset generators - anything that can benefit from a canvas and batch of controls
